sources.entry: Qwen Scribe - Private, local transcription and system-wide dictation for Apple Silicon, powered by Qwen3-ASR on MLX.

summary.one_liner: Qwen Scribe is a privacy-focused macOS app for Apple Silicon that transcribes audio and video locally with Qwen3-ASR on MLX, and offers system-wide push-to-talk dictation.
summary.what_it_does: Transcribes audio and video files through a local web interface with drag-and-drop, using Qwen3-ASR 1.7B or 0.6B models running on the Mac's Metal GPU via mlx-qwen3-asr. It supports automatic or forced language selection, vocabulary hints, word timestamps, and SRT export, and keeps a searchable local transcript history. A push-to-talk dictation helper records while a chosen modifier key is held, transcribes locally, and pastes the text at the cursor, with a menu-bar status item and a HUD. Files are queued one at a time, with cancel and retry. No account, API key, or cloud service is involved, and transcripts are stored as unencrypted JSON on the Mac.
use_cases: Transcribe meeting or interview recordings privately on a Mac
Generate SRT subtitles from video files offline
Dictate text into any app with a push-to-talk key
Batch-transcribe voice memos and audio files
Search and export a local history of transcripts
notable: Fully local: no account, API key, or cloud service; audio and transcripts stay on the Mac
System-wide push-to-talk dictation with a native macOS helper that restores the previous clipboard after pasting
Ships its own Python interpreter in the Mac app, so no Python install is needed to run it
Quantized 8-bit and 4-bit model variants can be prepared on the Mac from upstream weights
Localhost-only API with Host and browser-origin checks
caveats: Requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 14 or newer
Project is a beta (v0.3.0-beta.1); ad-hoc builds need manual approval in System Settings on first launch, and public Developer ID notarized binaries are not yet available
Requires Microphone, Input Monitoring, and Accessibility permissions for dictation; file transcription works without them
Files are capped at 4 GB, and ffmpeg is needed for AVI, Matroska, WebM, Ogg, Opus and WMA
